title: Making peace
hook: the clans of Mecca nearly fight over who sets the Black Stone, and Muhammad asks for a cloak: sulh, making peace between people
tomorrow: a man went to jail over a tax he refused to pay. why?

segments.voice: Yesterday's line: a share. Zacchaeus named his after Jesus came to dinner. Today, a fight over the one thing nobody wanted to share: an honor.
screen: `A SHARE.` → `NOW, AN HONOR NOBODY WILL SHARE.`

segments.voice: Two neighbors, one stairwell, and a bike and a stroller that both want the same corner. "Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the children of God," Jesus said. Islamic tradition tells of one in Mecca, years before the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, was called as a prophet. The clans of Quraysh are rebuilding the Kaaba. When it's time to set the Black Stone back in its place, every clan wants that honor for itself. They come close to war. The man chosen to settle it asks for something odd: a cloak.
screen: `A BIKE, A STROLLER, ONE CORNER.` → `BLESSED ARE THE PEACEMAKERS.` → `EVERY CLAN WANTS THE HONOR.` → `HE ASKS FOR A CLOAK.`

segments.voice: Why a cloak? The clans had agreed that the next man through the gate would judge. It was Muhammad, and they said: here is al-Amin, the trustworthy one; we accept him. He spreads out the cloak and sets the stone in the middle. Then he tells each clan to take hold of an edge, and together they lift it up to its place. Only then does he set it in the wall with his own hand. Puzzle solved. Nobody wins the honor alone, so nobody loses it. Everyone carries the stone. This is Islam's teaching of sulh: making peace between people. The Quran tells believers that they are brothers, so make peace between your brothers. And in a hadith in Abu Dawud, the Prophet asks: shall I tell you what is higher in rank than fasting, prayer and charity? Making peace between people. So a peacemaker, in this teaching, isn't the one who stays out of the fight. It's the one who steps in and finds a way for everyone to hold a corner.
screen: `AL-AMIN, THE TRUSTWORTHY.` · `THE STONE ON THE CLOAK.` · `EVERY CLAN LIFTS A CORNER.` · `SULH: HIGHER THAN FASTING.` · then, large: `PEACEMAKER.`

segments.voice: Hold your hands out in front of you, palms up, as if you're holding one edge of a cloak with others. Feel the weight shared. Bring to mind one conflict near you, and for the rest of the sit, look for the corner each person could hold.
Making peace: in Islam, sulh, setting things right between people, so that no one carries the stone alone.
Your line: peacemaker, the one who hands everyone a corner of the cloak to lift. Day 1731, done.

screen: `DAY 1731 COUNTS.` → `IN THE WORLD · 11 OF 14.` → `TOMORROW: A MAN WENT TO JAIL OVER A TAX HE REFUSED TO PAY. WHY?`

howItsDone: Muslims are taught to make peace between quarreling people (islah, sulh), and families and communities may ask a trusted elder to mediate. The story of the Black Stone and the cloak is told from the Prophet's biography.

sulh.meaning: peacemaking; setting things right between people
